title: DBMS & Data Warehousing
weightage: ~9-16 marks per paper (2024-2026 DA papers; trending upward - DA 2026 had ~10 DB/warehousing questions incl. SQL, RA, FDs, B+ tree, ER and data cube)
summary: Classic GATE DBMS core (ER, relational algebra/calculus, SQL output, FDs & normal forms, B+ tree indexing) plus DA-specific data preprocessing (min-max/z-score normalization, discretization, sampling) and warehouse modelling (star/snowflake schemas, data cubes, OLAP measures). Questions are mostly computational: evaluate a query on given tables, find keys/normal form, count B+ tree nodes, compute a cube aggregate.
notesGuide: 1) Core DBMS: download the db-book.com 7th-edition slide PDFs ch2 (relational model), ch3-4 (SQL, integrity constraints, data types), ch6 (ER), ch7 (normalization), ch13 (file organization), ch14 (indexing), ch27 (relational algebra & tuple calculus) and annotate them while watching Gate Smashers or NPTEL IIT-KGP lectures. 2) Keep CMU 15-445 lecture-note PDFs 01, 02, 05 (compression), 08-09 (B+ trees) as crisp secondary notes. 3) Warehousing/preprocessing: download Han-Kamber-Pei slides 03Preprocessing.ppt and 04OLAP.ppt from hanj.cs.illinois.edu and db-book ch11 (Data Analytics); condense into a 2-page sheet of formulas (min-max, z-score, decimal scaling, equal-width/equal-frequency binning, sampling types) and schema diagrams (star, snowflake, fact constellation), plus the distributive/algebraic/holistic measures table. 4) Make your own one-page cheat sheets: RA operator -> SQL equivalent; SQL NULL/aggregate/duplicate rules; closure/candidate-key algorithm + 1NF->BCNF test checklist + lossless/dependency-preserving tests; B/B+ tree order & fan-out formulas. 5) Practise SQL hands-on (SQLBolt, pgexercises) and evaluate every PYQ query on its sample tables by hand, recording mistakes in an error log.
